title: Incident response
text:
NorthstarOps classifies a complete service outage as a SEV-1 incident. The incident commander must acknowledge a SEV-1 page within 12 minutes. Customer-facing status updates are published every 25 minutes until recovery.

After a SEV-1 incident, the incident commander schedules a review within four business days. The review must record the timeline, contributing factors, and follow-up owners.

title: Backup and restoration
text:
Production database backups run at 02:30 UTC every day. Encrypted backup copies are retained for 35 days. Backup files are stored in the isolated Boreal archive.

The recovery-time objective for the order service is 90 minutes. The recovery-point objective is 20 minutes. The platform team conducts a restoration drill every quarter.

title: Release approval
text:
A standard production release requires approval from one service owner and one independent reviewer. The release checklist includes a rollback plan and a successful staging smoke test.

The standard production release window is Tuesday and Thursday from 09:00 to 11:00 UTC. Emergency releases require incident-commander approval and a documented reason for bypassing the window.

title: Temporary access
text:
Temporary production access expires after eight hours. Access requests must identify a ticket number, a business purpose, and the approving service owner. Shared accounts are prohibited.

Break-glass access is reviewed by the security lead within one business day. The requester must attach the session log to the incident record.

title: Customer support routing
text:
The NorthstarOps support queue is named Harbor Desk. Standard customer requests receive an initial response within six business hours. Billing questions are assigned to the account-operations team.

Support coverage runs from 07:00 to 19:00 UTC on weekdays. Outside those hours, only production outages trigger the on-call rotation.

title: Data retention
text:
Application debug logs are retained for 14 days. Security audit events are retained for 180 days. Reports exported for a support case must be deleted 21 days after the case closes.

Customer deletion requests are recorded in the privacy queue. The privacy owner confirms completion within 28 calendar days. This fictional procedure does not describe legal requirements.

title: Capacity monitoring
text:
The platform team reviews capacity every Wednesday. A capacity investigation starts when CPU utilization stays above 75 percent for 15 consecutive minutes.

The normal target for free database storage is at least 30 percent. A storage alert opens when free space remains below 18 percent for ten minutes.

title: Supplier onboarding
text:
A new production supplier requires a security questionnaire and an assigned internal owner. The procurement team records the supplier in the Meridian register before activation.

Supplier access is reviewed every 60 days. A supplier that has no active internal owner is suspended until ownership is restored.

title: Archived backup procedure
text: Archived and superseded procedure: backup copies are retained for seven days. Production backups run at 05:00 UTC.
